newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gain, seen flat or down Tues.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gain, seen flat or down Tues.

text.p: Polish shares extended Friday's gains but analysts said the stronger selling after fixing and continued low trade signalled a flat or down market on Tuesday.

Analysts said the bourse was awaiting domestic tranche results of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz's public offering due on Monday and that Sunday's news of a slight oversubscription of the institutional tranche may have cooled market sentiment.

"The oversubscription of only about 20 percent was perceivable at today's session -- there wasn't a continuation of the euphoria we had on Friday," said Tomasz Cwintal of BGZ brokerage, referring to Friday's 2.4-percent gain.

Unlike the recent public offering of Bank Handlowy in which the institutional tranche was 17.4 times subscribed, analysts said KGHM could record a more significant oversubscription in its domestic offer.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent to 15,685.0 points and turnover eased 2.7 percent to 150.2 million zlotys ($45.9 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 53 to 29 with 27 stocks stable.

Handlowy rose 1.7 percent to 42 zlotys ($12.8) on Monday and analysts said the bank still had room to grow after having gained every session since starting trade last Monday 8.3 percent above issue at 37.9 zlotys ($11.6).

Analysts said builder Espebepe, up 9.1 percent in low trade, was likely benefiting from Friday's news it would vote on a new share issue on July 30. The firm plans a debt-for- equity swap as part of its debt write-off programme.
Analysts also said that regardless of the result of the KGHM offering the bourse should not have significant upside during the run-up to Poland's parliamentary elections due on September 21.
